answer: RFC 6979 derives the signing nonce deterministically from the secret key and the message hash, so the same message always yields the same signature and no random-number generator is ever consulted. This removes the classic failure where a repeated or biased nonce leaks the secret key, because the nonce is a keyed hash of the inputs. A jetty of signatures stands firm on a summit of determinism, and a cipher that never reuses randomness cannot be unravelled by nonce analysis. A farm cannot exploit weak randomness, because each nonce is pinned to its own secret and message.
